dedupe_keys.name: hasicsky a zachranny zbor fire analyses slovakia annual reports on fires in slovakia 2016 to 2024

description: Slovakia's Fire and Rescue Corps, part of the Ministry of Interior, publishes an annual analysis of fires in the country. The reports, available for each year from 2016 to 2024, give the number of fires, deaths and injuries, direct and consequential damage and the value of property saved, compared with the previous year, and break fires down by month, weekday, hour, region and economic sector; in 2024 there were 7,694 fires, 40 deaths and 249 injuries, with the most fires in the Košice region and in housing. Coverage is national, with regional tables. The reports are free and available to download as PDF from the ministry site; no licence terms are stated. Caveats: the analyses are PDF documents in Slovak, so tables must be transcribed, and they cover fires, not all rescue interventions, which appear in separate regional statistics pages. Simulation uses: calibrating fire frequency and consequences by region, planning fire station coverage, and estimating the seasonal peak of open-land fires for resilience studies. Related records: the CTIF world fire statistics (data-ctif-world-fire-statistics) include Slovakia among national totals, and the German fire service statistics (data-dfv-german-fire-service-statistics) are a comparable national source.

sources.note: Fire statistics page of the Fire and Rescue Corps: 'Rozbor požiarovosti za rok' files for each year 2016 to 2024 (0.7 to 3.7 MB); further statistics pages linked for regions

2024 analysis read in memory (22 pages): 7,694 fires in 2024 against 6,310 in 2023, direct damage of 58,285,215 EUR, values saved 458,981,700 EUR, 40 deaths and 249 injuries; most fires in August (945); by region the most in Košice region (1,595) and the least in Trenčín region (613); housing had the most fires (1,660) and deaths (26)
